title: Floe official Skill dependency declaration v2 (references/dependencies.json)
description: Author-facing documentation of schemaVersion 2. The native strict decoder in FloeAgent/Sources/FloeSkills/SkillDependency.swift is the authority. V2 keeps the SAME top-level, profile and requirement key sets, exact pins, pip lock/integrity rules and limits as v1, and adds exactly one new target value: profiles may target `macos` with `pip` and `npm` requirements only. apt, font and runtimeComponent stay Linux-only and fail closed on macOS; v1 remains Linux-only and unchanged. The file still lives inside the canonical Skill package at references/dependencies.json, so the signed contentDigest covers its bytes and every referenced lock; old clients treat it as inert data, and a client that does not yet decode v2 fails the provisioning channel closed. Every v2 declaration must keep the package's EXISTING hub-entry minimumAppVersion at 1.7.65 or newer (first capable candidate); the declaration itself has no version field. Adding fields requires a new schemaVersion and a capable native build.

schemaVersion.description: Parser compatibility version only. This document describes exactly 2; schemaVersion 1 remains its own frozen Linux-only schema. This is NOT the Skill package version: floe.json id/version remain the single user-visible package authority.

profiles.description: Dependency profiles. Provisioning selects the profile that matches the task's ACTUAL resolved target OS and architecture; there is no user target picker and task execution is never rerouted.

os.description: Linux target. V2 Linux profiles keep every v1 requirement kind and rule.

requirements.description: Linux profiles may use pip, apt, npm, font and runtimeComponent exactly as in v1.

os.description: The real macOS host target reached through the existing Mac bridge/SSH execution route. No Homebrew auto-install and no Debian package manager are implied.

requirements.description: macOS profiles accept ONLY pip and npm. apt, font and runtimeComponent fail closed because they are Debian/Linux resources; there is no silent substitution with another host package manager.

architectures.description: Architecture SELECTION, not documentation: provisioning matches these against the actual resolved target architecture. `any` participates on every architecture. Declare what the target really runs (for macOS, arm64 and/or x86_64; riscv64 only describes a Linux guest).

pipName.description: PyPI distribution name; extras, ranges, URLs, paths and VCS references are rejected.

pipVersion.description: One exact PEP 440 version. Provisioning installs name==version only; no operators, ranges or 'latest'. The pin must contain a digit (floating aliases like 'latest' never pass). The pip lock rules are unchanged on macOS and Linux: a declared lock must be a package-local references/...txt file whose bytes are covered by the package digest.

aptVersion.description: Exact Debian version, epoch preserved; +dfsg/-rev/+tilde suffixes stay part of the pin. The version body (after any epoch) must contain a digit, so floating aliases like 'latest' or '1:latest' never pass. Linux profiles only (apt and font).

npmVersion.description: Exact semver. Managed npm provisioning is exact name@version with real readback; a packaged package-lock.json is review evidence and is never replayed as an install.

fontIdentity.description: Exactly one Debian font package identity plus the shared exact Debian version pin; Linux profiles only.

lockfile.description: Package-local pip lock reference inside the signed archive. The lock lists wheel names with sha256 digests; its bytes are covered by the package contentDigest, so review binding covers the lock without external hashes. No path traversal. Same rule on Linux and macOS profiles.

componentDescriptorPath.description: The frozen runtime-component descriptor path. Identity, version, artifact sha256 and size come from the pinned descriptor through the existing managed runtime-component allowlist; the allowlist, the component-only cap and the nonblocking hook are NOT broadened here. Linux profiles only.

purpose.description: Short model-safe rationale shown in skill.read; never a command.

required.description: true: that skill's dependency-aware exec.shell invocation is refused with the honest reason while the requirement is not verified ready (ordinary shell commands without skillID keep working). false: execution proceeds with a visible annotation.
